The structure is described in space group Amm2, number 38, with Hall symbol A 2 -2. The input cell is monoclinic with lattice parameters a = 5.57063248 Å, b = 5.54794001 Å, c = 6.8639738 Å, α = 90°, β = 66.05950122°, and γ = 90°, and it contains 14 atoms with the declared composition Sr₃Nd₁Cu₁Ru₁O₈. All positional values are fractional, and the input coordinates were rounded to six decimal places before any corrections were applied.

The supplied standard and input frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s. Here P is the matrix whose first row is (0, -1, 0), whose second row is (-1, 6.333954988018424 × 10⁻¹⁷, -0.5), and whose third row is (-5.656038856281542 × 10⁻¹⁸, -3.3837351700940453 × 10⁻¹⁸, -0.5). The origin shift s is (0, 4.999999999588667 × 10⁻⁷, 4.999999999588667 × 10⁻⁷). This transformation is part of the structural definition and is required to recover the original input cell from the standard setting.

In the standard frame, strontium occupies three independent two-fold orbits. One Sr orbit is on Wyckoff site 2b with representative position (1/2, 0, z) and z = 0.8564995. A second Sr orbit is on 2a at (0, 0, z) with z = 0.35435699999999987. A third Sr orbit is again on 2b at (1/2, 0, z), now with z = 0.14193099999999997. Neodymium occupies a single 2a orbit at (0, 0, z) with z = 0.637861. Copper is also on a 2a orbit, with representative (0, 0, z) and z = 0.9947569999999999. Ruthenium occupies a 2b orbit at (1/2, 0, z) with z = 0.4964684999999999.

Oxygen is distributed over five independent orbits. The only general-position oxygen orbit is the 8f site with representative (x, y, z) = (0.2480420000000001, 0.24073049999999996, 0.5070324999999999), giving eight symmetry-related atoms. The remaining oxygen atoms lie on two-fold special positions: one 2a orbit at (0, 0, z) with z = 0.16523049999999995, one 2b orbit at (1/2, 0, z) with z = 0.6634684999999999, another 2b orbit at (1/2, 0, z) with z = 0.33927049999999986, and a final 2a orbit at (0, 0, z) with z = 0.8220319999999999. Together these multiplicities account for the full 14-atom input cell.

Several very small precision corrections are part of the real input geometry and must be preserved rather than idealized away. A strontium atom initially given at (0.8565, 0.5, 0.287002) is shifted by (-1.0000000000287557 × 10⁻⁶, 0, 0). Another strontium at (0.141931, 0.5, 0.716139) is shifted by (-1.000000000001 × 10⁻⁶, 0, 0). The ruthenium atom at (0.496469, 0.5, 0.007064) is shifted by (-9.999999999732445 × 10⁻⁷, 0, 0). An oxygen atom at (0.165231, 0.0, 0.66954) is shifted by (-1.000000000001 × 10⁻⁶, 0, 0), and another oxygen at (0.663469, 0.5, 0.673064) is shifted by (-1.0000000000287557 × 10⁻⁶, 0, 0). These displacements are minute, but they belong to the supplied input structure and distinguish it from a perfectly rounded idealization.
